setlist_extra.title: This Could Be The Last Time

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Black Peter** (4 reviews): Called the show's highlight, heating up notably in the closing jam; nothing else matches it; Considered one of the best Vince-era versions, and a really strong rendition overall [11][15][16][17]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Reviewer rates this version very good, among the show's highlights [12]
- **He's Gone** (1 other source): Listed as flowing through a jam into Drums, with another jam after before The Last Time [1]
- **Knockin' On Heaven's Door** (1 other source): Listed as the encore [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1993-01-24.142855.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 16 songs; 144 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd93-01-24.sbd.seff.5610.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 16 songs; 144 min; rated 2.94/5 by 17 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls it a great recording, with Bobby prominent in the mix and Jerry's voice sounding good; Reviewer says the sound is great and Jerry's voice is mostly together [11][15]
- **gd1993-01-24.set2.fob.schoeps.unknown.swayne.85009.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 12 songs; 94 min; rated 3.5/5 by 6 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the highs a bit glassy on this audience recording; the set improves as it goes; Slight, subtle mic repositioning occurs at the start of Playin'; the flaws are minor and affect little of the signal [6][16]
- **gd1993-01-24.142856.sbd.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 16 songs; 147 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended while at odds with his girlfriend over staying with the people who offered free Bay Area housing [10]
- Reviewer got tickets for all three shows of the run from one person in the parking lot [12]
- Reviewer brought his parents to their first show; his father praised Vince's keyboard playing, which was consistently good [13]
- Bobby's guitar tone is said to resemble his sound on 12/6/92 [11]
- Mellow feel is described as typical of early-nineties openers of a run [12]
- First half is described as low key; the second half is a good cooker [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1993-01-24.142855.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Dat Master (Panasonic SV-3700) > Dat Clone (44.1k) [1]. Also: Uploader credits David Gans for providing the tapes behind this soundboard source [1]
- **gd93-01-24.sbd.seff.5610.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > DAT > C > DAT > CDR > TAE (overlap) > WAV > SHN [3]
- **gd1993-01-24.set2.fob.schoeps.unknown.swayne.85009.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Scott Swayne; source: FOB Schoeps MK4s -> Panasonic sv255 -> (clone) Teac DA-P20 [6]. Also: Audience recording that reviewer found an upgrade over his own incomplete cassette copy; A 48k original transfer is available; uploader believes recordings of the rest of the run exist [6][17]
- **gd1993-01-24.142856.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Dat Master > Cassette Master (Tascam 122mkIII/TDK SA-X100) [2]
